column5: Divides the displayed integer by ten, selects the remainder from the digit atlas and walks the cursor left by the glyph width. This identifies the target independently of either panel draw call.
Reads width, height and UV corners from the atlas record and passes its four bounds to the batch writer. Recovered in src/native.c.
Writes event and value into the output arrays and advances their count. The same entry point is reconstructed and checked in src/native.c.
Stores both endpoints, duration, curve type, initial value and completion flag. The same routine starts the ready overlay fade from the touch handler.
Frees each frame sequence and deletes the ten animation slot objects when present. The base sprite vtable's non-deleting destructor branches here.
Initializes the four score thresholds, count, label visibility and tween. Its compiled armv7s function independently matches before relocation.
Draws decimal digits right to left, gives 1 a four-pixel advance and uses width minus two for all other digits. The floating number's vtable draw method calls it.
The four pointers after the zero offset and RTTI fields target the ready update, draw and destructor pair. Draw uses text_ready and tutorial.
The four methods after the two-word ABI header target game-over update, draw and the two destructors. Its update starts the score panel with thresholds 10, 20, 30 and 40.
Sets the finished flag and initial value at offsets 0x24 and 0xc. This function is independently verified in src/native.c.
The table after its two header words references sparkle pool update and draw, which gate on offsets 0x56 and 0x57, followed by both destructors.
The adjacent table references the node pool update and draw that gate on offsets 4 and 5, followed by both destructors.
Restores the sparkle pool vtable and disposes every object through its deleting destructor, then frees the element array.
Restores the floating-number pool vtable and disposes every item through its deleting destructor before freeing the array.
Vtable entries are the sparkle update, inherited sprite renderer, destructor pair and coordinate-reset method.
The vtable entries point to the random sparkle emitter, medal atlas draw routine and destructor pair.
The table points to the three-phase panel update and draw routine that uses two decimal readouts.
Looks up the blink atlas frames and creates their five-frame animation. Its own constructor reproduces the fields and initialization sequence.
The five-word 0,1,2,1,0 blink sequence is the only matching array outside the 12-integer bird flap table independently referenced by the bird constructor.
Two zero ABI header words precede the four independently matched floating-number update, draw, complete destructor and deleting destructor pointers.
